key_insight: Image-to-Video Transfer (I2VT) uses an image editor to improve pretrained video editors and extend them to new editing tasks—without collecting new paired source and edited videos.
problem_solved: Video editing models lag behind image editors partly because paired video-editing examples are difficult to collect. I2VT addresses how to transfer image-editing capabilities to video models without this additional data.
method: Use an image editor as the source of editing capabilities.
Transfer those capabilities to a pretrained video editor through efficient post-training.
Improve existing editing abilities and introduce new tasks without new paired video data.
impact: I2VT offers a path to broader video-editing capabilities with less dependence on costly paired-video collection. This could make adapting pretrained video editors more practical for AI/ML teams.
visual_elements: Transfer diagram: image editor → I2VT post-training → enhanced video editor.
Data comparison: paired source/edited videos marked as unnecessary for the new post-training process.

Capability diagram showing existing video-editing tasks alongside newly enabled tasks.
paper_title: Improving and Expanding Video Editing Capabilities Without Videos
paper_authors: Ji Xie, Yanhao Jia, Xiangpeng Yang, Martin Q. Ma, Sihan Xu
